title: Build a Business Cash-Flow Control System
hook: Profit on paper does not pay this week's obligations.
outcome: A weekly view of available cash, committed outflows, receivables, and runway.
steps: Separate business and personal accounts and define who can move money.
Track opening cash, posted inflows, posted outflows, upcoming obligations, receivables, and restricted funds.
Reconcile bank and processor activity instead of relying only on invoices.
Create thresholds for taxes, payroll, operations, refunds, reserves, and owner draws.
Review weekly and document any assumption, missing account, pending item, or stale data.
cta: Save this and build your cash view before your next sale.
disclaimer: Educational only. Cash-flow treatment, taxes, and accounting requirements vary by business and jurisdiction.

title: Price for Delivery, Risk, and Growth
hook: A price can look high and still leave the business broke.
outcome: A pricing floor and target built from real delivery economics.
steps: Calculate direct labor, contractors, software, materials, payment fees, support, rework, and delivery overhead.
Add sales cost, administrative capacity, taxes, bad debt, and a risk allowance.
Set a minimum gross-margin requirement and a capacity limit.
Compare price to the customer's alternative and value, then define scope and change control.
Review actual margin after delivery and update assumptions.
cta: Comment PRICE for the pricing worksheet.
disclaimer: Pricing must comply with applicable laws and contracts. Value estimates are assumptions, not guaranteed customer results.

title: Build an Operating Reserve Before Growth Breaks You
hook: Growth increases timing risk before it increases safety.
outcome: A reserve policy tied to actual obligations and volatility.
steps: List essential monthly obligations and the costs of shutting down or pausing safely.
Measure how volatile collections, refunds, chargebacks, repairs, and customer concentration are.
Choose a reserve target range and define what qualifies as an emergency use.
Move reserve funds into a separate, appropriately insured account with controlled access.
Review the policy after major contracts, hiring, debt, or cost changes.
cta: Save this before increasing fixed expenses.
disclaimer: Educational only, not individualized financial advice. Consider liquidity, insurance limits, taxes, and professional guidance.

title: Build a Funding-Ready Data Room
hook: Capital gets slower and more expensive when your records cannot survive questions.
outcome: A secure, current evidence package for lenders, grants, investors, or partners.
steps: Create an index covering entity documents, ownership, finances, taxes, contracts, customers, operations, security, and risks.
Reconcile financial statements to bank and processor evidence and explain unusual items.
Document use of funds, milestones, repayment or return logic, downside plan, and governance.
Use role-based access, expiration, watermarking where appropriate, and an access log.
Update the room monthly and remove obsolete or contradictory versions.
cta: Comment FUNDING for the data-room index.
disclaimer: Funding terms and disclosures can create legal and financial obligations. Use qualified advisors for actual transactions.
